verdict.rationale: Stripe Issuing is API-first. Its docs show card and cardholder creation, spending controls with per-authorization and monthly limits, API access to balance funding information, and transaction visibility for agents. A general Stripe MCP server lets agents interact with the Stripe API. However, the pack does not show updating cards, a transaction-read endpoint, Issuing-specific MCP tools, or scoped/restricted credentials for agents. missing for 10: evidence of scoped/restricted API keys for agents, explicit card-update and spend-control-update endpoints, transaction listing API, Issuing coverage in the MCP server, independent hands-on corroboration

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent can operate my card program — read balances and transactions, create and update cards, and adjust spend controls through the API or an MCP surface with scoped credentials

citations.quote: You can use spending controls to block merchant categories (for example, bakeries), countries, merchant IDs, or card presence, and to set spending limits per authorization or per month.
Using the Stripe Dashboard or API, you can access the bank account and routing information you need to push funds from your external bank account.
Issuing for agents lets you issue virtual cards that agents can use to make purchases autonomously, with spend controls, real-time authorization decisioning, and full transaction visibility.
The Stripe Model Context Protocol (MCP) server provides tools that AI agents can use to interact with the Stripe API
